q: Consider the Directive Principles: 1-They are not enforceable by any court. 2-They are fundamental in the governance of the country. 3-The State is under a duty to apply them in making laws. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three appear in the same article: non-enforceability, fundamentality and the duty to apply.
why: Candidates reject the second and third because the first is so firmly learned. The same article carries all three propositions together.
trapnote: Non-enforceable does not mean irrelevant. The same article that denies the remedy asserts the duty.

q: A free legal aid claim is made by an indigent accused. Consider: 1-The directive on legal aid is by itself enforceable. 2-It becomes enforceable when read with the right to life. 3-It is implemented through a statutory legal services framework. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: A directive alone gives no remedy; the enforceability comes from reading it into the liberty guarantee.
why: This is the central mechanism of the whole Part: a directive acquires teeth only through a fundamental right, never on its own.
trapnote: Whenever a directive is said to be enforceable, look for the fundamental right it was read into.

q: Which grouping correctly reflects the conventional classification of the Directive Principles?
options: Uniform civil code, environment and separation of powers fall in the Gandhian group
Equal pay, legal aid and living wage fall in the Gandhian group
Village panchayats, legal aid and monuments fall in the Gandhian group
Village panchayats, cottage industry and cow protection fall in the Gandhian group
expl: The Gandhian group centres on village self-rule, cottage industry, weaker sections and cattle.
why: The distractors each mix one genuine Gandhian item with liberal or socialist items, so partial recognition is not enough.
trapnote: Classify by theme: village and rural economy is Gandhian; wages and welfare are socialist; law reform is liberal.

q: On the shield protecting certain laws from challenge, which statement is correct?
options: It protects laws giving effect to any directive in the Part
It protects laws giving effect to two specified directives only
It protects laws giving effect to any directive, if Parliament so declares
It protects laws giving effect to two directives, only against the equality guarantee
expl: The attempt to widen the shield to all directives was struck down; two clauses remain.
why: The fourth option is the subtle one: the shield operates against both the equality and freedom guarantees, not equality alone.
trapnote: Two limbs to check: which directives are covered, and which rights the shield operates against.

q: Consider the amendment that dealt with education: 1-It inserted a fundamental right to education for the six to fourteen age group. 2-It reworded the directive on early childhood care. 3-It added a fundamental duty on parents. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: One amendment touched Part III, Part IV and Part IVA simultaneously.
why: Candidates usually recall only the new fundamental right and treat the other two limbs as belonging to different amendments.
trapnote: This amendment is unusual in touching three Parts at once. Expect all three limbs in a set question.

q: On Fundamental Duties, which statement is correct?
options: Eleven were introduced in 1976 and none has been added since
Ten were introduced in 1976 and an eleventh was added in 2005
Ten were introduced in 1976 and an eleventh was added in 2002
Eleven were introduced in 1976 and a twelfth was added in 2002
expl: The original set was ten; the parental duty on schooling was the eleventh addition.
why: All four options are numerically close, so recognition of the familiar figure eleven does not by itself identify the right answer.
trapnote: Separate the original count from the later addition. Both numbers are asked, often in the same option.

q: Consider: 1-Fundamental Duties are enforceable by writ. 2-They may be enforced through ordinary legislation. 3-Courts use them to interpret the scope of rights. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: No writ lies for a duty, but statutes enforce them and courts use them interpretively.
why: The distinction between direct enforceability and indirect operation through statute and interpretation is the whole of this topic.
trapnote: Unenforceable by writ is not the same as legally inert. Duties operate through statutes and interpretation.

q: A State enacts prohibition, relying on the directive concerning intoxicating drinks. A trader challenges it. Which statement is correct?
options: The directive by itself validates the law, the freedom yielding to it
The directive supports the restriction, which must still be reasonable
The directive is irrelevant, being unenforceable in a court of law
The directive validates the law only if the shield is expressly invoked
expl: Directives inform the reasonableness of a restriction without overriding the right.
why: Two of the wrong options represent the two opposite errors: treating directives as supreme, and treating them as legally worthless.
trapnote: Directives neither override rights nor are irrelevant to them. They inform reasonableness.

q: Which article provides for the separation of the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State?
options: A directive in the liberal group, which underlies the split in the magistracy
A directive in the Gandhian group, which underlies village-level adjudication
A fundamental right, breach of which is directly actionable by writ
A directive in the socialist group, which underlies the legal aid framework
expl: It is a liberal-group directive and the source of the judicial and executive magistrate split.
why: The practical consequence, remand before one magistrate and preventive orders before another, is what makes this directive operationally important.
trapnote: This directive has a daily consequence in policing: two kinds of magistrate, two kinds of order.

q: Consider the 2024 ruling on material resources of the community: 1-It narrowed the meaning of the directive. 2-It held that private ownership alone determines the question. 3-It confirmed the continued operation of the unamended shield. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The ruling narrowed the directive and preserved the unamended shield, rejecting ownership as the test.
why: The second statement inverts the holding: the Court rejected the proposition that every privately owned resource qualifies.
trapnote: Where a ruling narrows a provision, expect a statement that overstates it in the opposite direction.

q: A State claims that any welfare law is immune from challenge because it advances a Directive Principle. Which is the correct objection?
options: The shield requires the prior approval of the President before it operates
The shield operates only where the law was enacted by Parliament and not a State
The shield was abolished entirely, no such immunity surviving today
The shield is confined to two directives, and welfare generally is not among them
expl: The wide version of the shield was struck down; the narrow version survives for two clauses.
why: The fourth option overcorrects, which is a common error once a candidate learns that the shield was cut back.
trapnote: Cutting a provision down is not abolishing it. Identify precisely how far the narrowing went.

q: Consider the directive on equal pay and the duty to develop a scientific temper. Which statement is correct?
options: Both are directives, the second falling in the liberal group
The first is a directive and the second a fundamental duty
Both are fundamental duties, the first added in 2002
The first is a fundamental duty and the second a directive
expl: Equal pay for equal work is a directive; scientific temper is a duty of the citizen.
why: The two Parts are adjacent and thematically similar, which is why swap questions between them are common.
trapnote: Directives bind the State; duties bind the citizen. Ask who the provision addresses.

q: A parent refuses to send a nine-year-old to school. Which combination correctly identifies the provisions engaged?
options: A fundamental right of the child and a fundamental duty of the parent
A fundamental right of the child and a directive addressed to the parent
A directive on early childhood care and a fundamental duty of the parent
A fundamental duty of the child and a directive addressed to the State
expl: The child holds the right; the parent bears the corresponding duty.
why: The third option is attractive because the early childhood directive exists, but it concerns children below six, not a nine-year-old.
trapnote: Match the age to the provision. Below six is a directive; six to fourteen is a right.

q: Consider: 1-The uniform civil code directive is in the liberal group. 2-The village panchayats directive is in the Gandhian group. 3-The legal aid directive was inserted in 2002. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Legal aid was inserted in 1976, not 2002; the two group assignments are correct.
why: Two accurate pairings are placed beside one accurate-looking date error, so group knowledge alone will not settle the set.
trapnote: Do not assume every set contains an error. Verification is faster than suspicion.

q: An officer refuses to arrange legal aid for an indigent arrested person, citing budgetary constraint. Which statement is correct?
options: The obligation is unenforceable, the directive being outside the reach of courts
The obligation arises only after the accused is committed to trial by a magistrate
The obligation rests on the legal services authority alone and not on the police
The obligation is enforceable, the directive having been read into the liberty guarantee
expl: Legal aid to an indigent accused is an enforceable component of the liberty guarantee.
why: The fourth option shifts the duty to another agency, which is a realistic field argument and therefore a strong distractor.
trapnote: Where a directive has been read into a right, the resulting obligation binds every State agency, including the police.

q: On the relationship between Parts III and IV, which statement is correct?
options: Part IV prevails over Part III wherever a conflict arises
The balance between them is itself part of the basic structure
Part III prevails absolutely, Part IV yielding in every case
Neither Part may be amended, both being beyond the amending power
expl: Giving either Part absolute primacy was held to destroy an essential feature.
why: The second and third options represent the two positions the courts rejected at different times, which is why both feel historically familiar.
trapnote: Both extremes have been argued and both were rejected. The answer is the balance itself.

q: Consider the directives inserted in 1976: 1-Legal aid. 2-Participation of workers in management. 3-Protection of the environment. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three were inserted by the same 1976 amendment.
why: Candidates often attribute the environmental directive to a later amendment because environmental law developed afterwards.
trapnote: Three directives entered together in 1976. Learn them as a single group.

q: Which statement about the directive on promotion of cooperative societies is correct?
options: It was inserted in 1976, alongside the directives on legal aid and environment
It was inserted in 2002, alongside the change to early childhood care
It was inserted in 2011, alongside a related change to the freedom of association
It was inserted in 2011, alongside a related change to the right to property
expl: The cooperatives amendment added a directive and extended the freedom of association.
why: Two options give the correct year with a wrong companion change, so the year alone does not decide the question.
trapnote: Amendments usually make several changes at once. Learn the package, not the isolated item.

q: A law reserving seats in local bodies for weaker sections is challenged as unequal. Which statement is correct?
options: A directive on weaker sections overrides the equality guarantee entirely
The shield protects it from any challenge on grounds of inequality
The challenge succeeds, directives having no bearing on the equality analysis
A directive on weaker sections supports it, and equality permits reasonable classification
expl: The directive informs the reasonableness of the classification without displacing the guarantee.
why: The third option misapplies the shield, which does not extend to the directive on weaker sections at all.
trapnote: Check whether the shield actually covers the directive relied on before treating a law as immune.

q: Consider: 1-Directives were drawn from the Irish Constitution. 2-Fundamental Duties were recommended by the Sarkaria Commission. 3-Environmental protection appears both as a directive and as a duty. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Duties came from the Swaran Singh Committee; Sarkaria dealt with Centre-State relations.
why: The environment appears twice over, as a directive binding the State and a duty binding the citizen, which is the point worth retaining.
trapnote: Some subjects appear in both Part IV and Part IVA. The environment is the clearest example.
